nodes.text: Oh — welcome, welcome. Mind the sawdust. Actually, no, don't — sawdust on the floor means work on the bench. I'm *Tilo*. The loom, the carving bench, the worktable — all public, all yours. Sorry, I should let you speak.
What can I do for you?

choices.text: Public? Anyone can use these stations?
Your sister says you never finish anything.
You trained somewhere grand, I'd guess.

nodes.text: Anyone with the patience. That's the whole idea — a croft can't afford a loom, but a *town* can afford one everybody shares. Bring hide, cloth, or timber. Leave with something that didn't exist at breakfast. There's no better feeling. Well — one, maybe. Finishing. I'm told.

Merra told you about the chair. Of course she did. Three years — yes. Three years. But the chair is *teaching* me, you see. Every joint I cut for pay, I cut better, because the chair at home is watching. …That sounded less strange in my head. Most true things do.

Silverfall's galleria — a clothier took me on as a boy to carry bolts up the Silver Stair. I came down before the deep trouble with one pattern-book and a needle case. The mountain teaches you the *grand* way to do things. The ford taught me the useful way. Between the two you get a decent craftsman.
Leather, cloth, and woodcraft patterns — the whole soft-trades ladder. Priced by what they'll ask of your hands.
